subject: Qualification follow-up: SLO scope, benchmark procedures, and open items
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Gael Rios <gael@cartwheel.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Qualification recap + proposed benchmark plan

Hi Gael —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist before we start the measurement work: 

1) SLOs we discussed
   - P50 latency (token-complete): 120ms target, 200ms SLA floor
   - P95 latency (token-complete): 350ms target, 500ms SLA floor
   - Throughput target: 150 requests/sec sustained per endpoint during peak shopping hours
   - Concurrent inference sessions: up to 180 concurrent streaming sessions with average per-session QPS of ~0.8

2) Streaming specifics
   - Clients will open a streaming connection and expect incremental tokens every ~50–80ms once generation starts. We should measure tail token inter-arrival for 95th/99th percentiles.
   - Session warm-up: KV cache priming will be minimal; we should run cold-start vs warmed runs.

3) Benchmark methodology (high-level)
   - We'll run three passes: cold (no cache), warmed (primed KV), and production-mix (latency/throughput profile synthetic traffic).
   - Prompt inventory (attached) will be used as the canonical prompt set — please flag any PII or redactions needed.
   - Measurement definitions: per-message token-complete latency; per-token interp-arrival for streaming; percent of requests exceeding SLA.

4) Next steps / asks from Cartwheel
   - Confirm prompt inventory is representative (reply inline).
   - Share a small sample of production RTT traces if possible (sanitized).
   - Confirm preferred windows for a 4-hour benchmark run (we suggested Thu 3/11 02:00–06:00 PST).

Attachments: prompt_inventory_v1.csv (text/csv), harness_instructions.md (text/markdown)

I will schedule a short kickoff once we get your confirmation and we’ll loop in Engineering (Kim) to finalize run orchestration.

Best,

Nikhil Sharma
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai

From: Gael Rios <gael@cartwheel.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 12:37:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Qualification recap + proposed benchmark plan

Thanks Nikhil — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the 120ms P50 is aggressive but aligns with our internal goals. Can you confirm whether that’s measured end-to-end (client RTT) or server-side token-complete only? We can provide client-side traces, but I think server-side token-complete is fair for initial runs.

- Streaming: we care more about the first-token latency and steady-state token inter-arrival. For some assistants, token jumps >150ms are user-visible regressions.

- Concurrency: our peak plan (holiday load) expects short bursts to 300 concurrent sessions; 180 is our baseline steady-state. Can Redwood simulate sudden ramp + backoff (we need to see how graceful degradation works).

- Prompt inventory: reviewed quickly — there are ~12 prompts referencing order IDs. We’ll provide a sanitized copy by EOD.

As for the window, Thu 3/11 02:00–06:00 PST works for us, but we prefer a later backup window Fri 3/12 22:00–02:00 PST in case we need extra cycles.

Thanks — I’ll have procurement loop in if we move toward a formal onboarding run.

—Gael
Head of Platform, Cartwheel Retail
gael@cartwheel.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Gael Rios <gael@cartwheel.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Qualification recap + proposed benchmark plan

Gael / Nikhil —

I’m Kim (Runtime Engineering). A couple of operational notes before the run: 

- Measurement hooks: we will expose server-side token-complete timestamps and per-token timestamps via the harness. Please confirm you are OK with server-side metrics for the first pass.

- Ramp simulation: we have a stress harness that can apply different ramp shapes (instant, linear 30s, exponential). We’ll plan an instant-to-peak ramp and a 10-minute cool-down to surface degradation modes.

- Warm vs cold runs: to be explicit, cold = empty KV + cold GPU kernels (simulate cold container), warmed = KV preloaded with two recent conversations per prompt.

- Artifacts I’m attaching: harness_instructions.md (how to run), benchmark_run_template.xlsx (run matrix), and a short checklist for reproducibility (what to capture: seed, model hash, quantization flags).

Attachments: harness_instructions.md (text/markdown), benchmark_run_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

If you can confirm the permissable data mask for prompts we’ll finalize the prompt inventory and schedule pre-checks on Wed 3/10.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Runtime Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Gael Rios <gael@cartwheel.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Qualification recap + proposed benchmark plan

Gael — thanks for the details and for flagging the burst behavior. Quick confirmations and a modest tweak to the plan: 

- Latency definitions: we’ll publish server-side token-complete and first-token metrics in the report. If you provide client RTT traces we’ll include them as an appendix but won’t use them for pass/fail gating on the first run.

- Concurrency/burst: we will include one deliberate burst stage to 320 concurrent sessions for 3 minutes mid-run to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies. That will also exercise routing fallback (region/variant).

- Data & prompt sanitization: thanks — once we get the sanitized prompt set we’ll run an automated PII check and share a redaction log.

- Scheduling: Wed 3/10 16:00–17:00 PST for a short pre-check (30min) + Thu 3/11 02:00–06:00 PST for the full run (backup Fri 3/12 22:00–02:00 PST).

Links / artifacts:
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/12345
- Benchmark harness recipe: https://app.redwood.ai/harness/recipes/streaming-probe

Next steps (action owners):
- Gael: upload sanitized prompt set and optional client traces (due EOD Wed 3/10).
- Kim: prep run matrix and confirm ramp shapes (I think we are aligned).
- Vanessa: send calendar invites and reserve the bench infra slots.

I’ll kick off a shared Drive folder after this note and drop the final checklist there.

Thanks — Nikhil

From: Gael Rios <gael@cartwheel.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, procurement@acme-corp.com

Subject: Re: Qualification recap + proposed benchmark plan

All good from Cartwheel. We will:

- Send sanitized prompt_inventory_v1.csv by EOD.
- Include a 30s sample of client-side RTT traces (anonymized).
- Procurement (cc’d) will follow up on the onboarding form and SOC2 evidence; they might request the security questionnaire you attached.

Confirming the pre-check window Wed 3/10 16:00–17:00 PST and main window Thu 3/11 02:00–06:00 PST. If anything changes we’ll flag it immediately.

Best — Gael
